# Short-term forecasts

Catch advice is based on short-term forecasts: the stock is projected from the assessment through intermediate
years (status quo F or a known catch) into the advice year under alternative F (or catch) scenarios. With SS3 the
scenarios are run as forecasts in `forecast.ss` (fixed F by fleet and season, scaled from the F basis of the advice
to apical F; see the FLRef workflow and `ss3diags::SSnewrun()`), and the runs are read with `r4ss::SSgetoutput()`.
ss3diags2 takes it from there: `ss3_fwd()` converts the runs into `FLStockR` objects, `ss3plot_fwd()` plots the
scenarios with or without uncertainty, and `ss3_fwdtable()` summarises the fishing opportunities.

The example is the Adriatic hake (GSAs 17-18, reference year 2024) with three F scenarios run in SS3: the advice F
(Fadv), status quo F (Fsq) and no fishing (F0), after two intermediate years (2025-2026) at the recent catch. The
assessment report used throughout this guide (`hke.37.17-18.rds`) is the Fadv run, so it serves as the reference
model, and the scenarios are kept as their `r4ss::SSsummarize()` summary, which holds the derived quantities with
their standard errors in a fraction of the size:

```{r fwd}
fw <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "hke.37.17-18", "hke.37.17-18_fwd.rds", package = "ss3diags2"))
fw$modelnames
```

> **Not formal advice.** The reference points below are the model's own estimates (Btgt = SSB at B35%, Ftgt = the
> corresponding F, Bpa and Blim at 50% and 25% of Btgt); the forecasts illustrate the functions and are not the GFCM
> advice for this stock.

```{r fwd-stk}
fs  <- ss3_fwd(fw, Fref = "Btgt", bpa = 0.5, blim = 0.25)            # MLE and SE of each scenario
stk <- ss3stk(hke, Fref = "Btgt", bpa = 0.5, blim = 0.25)             # assessment (reference model)
fs[[1]]@refpts
```

```{r fwd-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
ss3plot_fwd(fs, stk = stk, ci = FALSE)
```

With uncertainty: the assessment from MVLN draws of the reference model, the scenarios from their standard errors:

```{r fwd-ci, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
stki <- ss3stk(hke, output = "iters", iters = 1000, Fref = "Btgt", bpa = 0.5, blim = 0.25)
ss3plot_fwd(fs, stk = stki)
```

The fishing opportunities table gives catch and F in the advice year (the first year in which the scenarios
differ, 2027), SSB at the start of the next year, its change from the advice year, and the probability of SSB below
Blim (lognormal with the SS3 standard error; from the draws when the full reports are used with
`ss3_fwd(output = "iters")`):

```{r fwd-table}
ss3_fwdtable(fs)
```

> **Reading the forecast plot.** The black line and bands are the assessment, the coloured lines the scenarios
> from the end year (2024, first dashed line) on. The second dashed line is the implementation (advice) year (2027);
> between the lines are the intermediate years (2025-2026), in which all scenarios take the same catch, so they
> overlap; they separate in the advice year. SSB responds one year
> later (SSB at the start of 2028 reflects the catch of 2027), which is why the table reports SSB of the year after
> the advice year. The horizontal lines are the benchmarks (Btgt green, Bpa orange, Blim red; Ftgt green).
